items.summary: President Trump posted a series of AI-generated images on Truth Social alongside threats directed at Iran, including one depicting himself as "Guardian of the World."
items.why_it_matters: A sitting president using AI-generated imagery in political communications on an official platform raises questions about norms for synthetic media in executive-branch political messaging.

items.title: StackAdapt Launches Political Targeting and Measurement Suite to Help Campaigns Optimize Voter Outreach Ahead of the 2026 Midterms
items.summary: StackAdapt, which describes itself as an AI advertising and orchestration platform, has launched a political targeting and measurement suite for the U.S. market, combining political audience creation, voter intelligence, campaign measurement, and ad optimization in a single workflow for political advertisers ahead of the 2026 midterms.
items.why_it_matters: A dedicated AI-powered political ad suite from an established programmatic platform expands the range of automated targeting tools available to campaigns and PACs at scale.

items.title: AI Deepfakes Are Official Campaign Strategy. The 2026 Midterms Proved It.
items.summary: RoboRhythms reports that AI-generated deepfakes have become an explicit campaign strategy in the 2026 midterms, noting that no federal law prohibits their use in political advertising.
items.why_it_matters: Documents the mainstreaming of synthetic media as a deliberate campaign tactic in a major election cycle, underscoring the gap in federal regulation.

items.title: How 20 States Are Now Regulating Deepfakes—and What It Means for Elections
items.summary: GovFacts surveys the patchwork of deepfake laws across states, noting 47 states have passed some form of deepfake legislation since 2019, while Alaska, Missouri, and Ohio have none, with significant variation in how election-related synthetic media is addressed and enforced.
items.why_it_matters: Illustrates the fragmented state-level regulatory landscape campaigns and vendors must navigate in 2026, complementing federal inaction.
